name: Aminata Diallo
action: Aminata keeps her voice even and says, "I’m sorry, Fatoumata, but I can’t give up my Sunday. I have to study for my exam."
reason: Aminata’s first impulse was to pull back, stay quiet, and avoid an immediate refusal while she felt the pull of family duty. Reflection strengthened her resistance to yielding by making the cost of losing Sunday more concrete—her Monday exam, the difficult depreciation work, and the savings she is protecting for her sister—while still leaving her unwilling to answer harshly. That is why her revised tendency becomes a calm, direct refusal rather than a silent retreat or an easy agreement. Her reserved, meticulous nature, her habit of guarding scarce time and plans, and her memories of how family obligations have previously disrupted work and security all make a polite but firm statement the most plausible immediate response, even though the obligation to Fatoumata remains a competing pressure.
